title: Market Surf Report

conditions.headline: Blue wave hits the beach, futures paddle higher
conditions.summary: Stock futures are higher after Democrats won control of the House and Senate, with chip earnings from AMD lifting tech. Early quotes are thin and vary by source, so expect some chop at the open.

sections.title: Futures & Overnight
items: As of about 4:25 AM CT, Dow futures were up 1.3%, S&P 500 futures up 0.9% and Nasdaq-100 futures up 0.9% (TipRanks); a later Yahoo snapshot showed smaller gains, so early quotes are thin.
Democrats won control of both the House and Senate, setting up a divided government.
The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.92%, and the dollar weakened overnight.
Gold jumped about 2.5% to near $4,050 an ounce; bitcoin bounced about 2% to roughly $78,500 after touching a seven-week low near $75,600.
WTI crude slipped 0.3% to $95.83 as Qatar mediates efforts to end the US-Israeli war with Iran.
Asia was mixed: Shanghai +2.2% and Hang Seng +1.7%, but Japan's Nikkei fell 1.4%.
Europe opened higher, with London's FTSE 100 up about 1.2% and renewables leading.

sections.title: Macro & Economic Calendar
items: 6:00 AM CT: MBA mortgage applications (prior +3.4%).
7:15 AM CT: ADP private payrolls for October, consensus about 67,000 to 70,000 vs 90,000 prior.
8:45 AM CT: S&P Global services PMI (final).
9:00 AM CT: ISM services PMI, consensus about 54.7 vs 54.9 prior.
9:30 AM CT: EIA weekly crude inventories.
No scheduled Fed speakers turned up in our sources; the main macro story is the midterm results and a split Congress.

sections.title: Earnings
items: AMD beat: adjusted EPS $2.09 vs $1.95 expected, revenue $13.4B (up about 45%) vs $13.1B; data center sales nearly doubled. Stock up about 6% pre-market.
Arista Networks beat on AI-driven growth; shares up about 9.5% pre-market.
Duolingo missed on EPS ($0.54 vs $0.57) but beat on revenue, grew daily users 29% and raised full-year guidance; shares up over 13% pre-market.
Novo Nordisk beat and raised its 2026 sales forecast on obesity-drug demand; shares up about 5%, per early reports.
Amdocs plunged over 40% pre-market on bleak guidance tied to a dispute with T-Mobile.
Also reporting today: McDonald's, Uber, CVS, McKesson, MetLife, Allstate, Kraft Heinz and MercadoLibre; Qualcomm and Arm are the headliners expected after the close.

sections.title: Stocks in the News
items: AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): +6% to +7% — quarterly beat on booming data center sales.
ANET (Arista Networks): +9.5% — earnings beat on AI networking demand.
SMCI (Super Micro Computer): +7.2% — riding the AI-hardware rally.
DUOL (Duolingo): +13% — strong user growth and raised guidance outweigh an EPS miss.
NVO (Novo Nordisk): +5% — beat and raised its 2026 sales outlook.
IONQ (IonQ): +6.5% — quantum stocks bounce.
DOX (Amdocs): -40% — weak outlook amid a T-Mobile dispute.
NVDA (Nvidia) and MU (Micron): down more than 1% — data center regulation worries after the elections.

sections.title: Business News
items: Democrats take both chambers of Congress, likely slowing parts of the White House agenda, including crypto legislation.
In Texas, Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the governor's race and has pledged a pause on new data center construction; Texas holds more than a quarter of planned US data center capacity.
Oracle reportedly scrapped a $7 billion AI chip leasing deal with Tencent amid US pressure.
Oil stays volatile on Iran war headlines, with Qatar mediating talks.
Bitcoin ETFs saw a third straight day of outflows, about $1.2 billion over three sessions.

sections.title: What to Watch Today
items: 7:15 AM CT ADP jobs and 9:00 AM CT ISM services for a read on the economy before Friday's jobs report.
Whether AI and chip stocks hold gains as investors weigh data center restrictions after the midterms.
Qualcomm and Arm results after the close.

script: Cowabunga! This is Surf Daddy, your local Kahuna, live from Surfside USA to all you Trade Wind surfers from the Gulf Coast to the North Shore. It's Wednesday, November fourth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Market Surf Report. Riding shotgun on the cabana deck is my co-anchor, Gus the wonder dog, still wagging from election night. Give the beach a big hello, Gus! Alright, let's check the swell. Stock futures are paddling higher on this Dawn Patrol. Early reads had Dow futures up about one point three percent, and S and P five hundred and Nasdaq futures up about nine tenths of a percent. A later snapshot showed smaller gains, so the early quotes are thin. The big story is the midterms. Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate. That means a divided government in Washington. The ten year Treasury yield eased to about four point nine two percent, and the dollar softened. Gold jumped about two and a half percent to near four thousand fifty dollars an ounce. Bitcoin bounced about two percent to around seventy eight thousand five hundred. Crude oil slipped to about ninety six dollars. Over in Asia, China rallied, but Japan's Nikkei fell. Europe opened higher. Now the wind and weather. At seven fifteen A M Central, we get the A D P private jobs report, with forecasts near seventy thousand. At nine A M Central, the I S M services survey is expected near fifty four point seven. On the tide chart, A M D crushed it last night. Data center sales nearly doubled, and the stock is up about six percent before the bell. That calls for a treat, Gus! Here you go, buddy! Arista Networks is hanging ten, up more than nine percent on strong A I demand. Super Micro is up about seven percent. Duolingo missed on profit but grew users fast, and the stock is up over thirteen percent. Novo Nordisk beat and raised its sales outlook. But Amdocs took a gnarly wipeout, down more than forty percent on a weak outlook tied to T Mobile. Some chip names like Nvidia and Micron are slipping. Why? In Texas, the new governor elect has pledged a pause on new data centers. That has A I builders watching the tide. And Oracle reportedly dropped a seven billion dollar chip leasing deal with Tencent. Sets to watch today. The jobs and services data this morning. Whether chip stocks hold their gains. And Qualcomm and Arm after the close. Soul surfers, stay calm when the water gets choppy. And hey, stoked to say you can look up any stock, E T F or futures contract in the Check a Wave box on the page, and Surf Daddy will call it for you. This is information, not advice. This is Surf Daddy and Gus the wonder dog saying, if in doubt, paddle out!
